Hi James / FinVault IT team —

Thanks for taking time today. Per our discovery call, we want to confirm a practical sequencing for SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and the IP allowlist cutover so your ops window is guaranteed and we have fallbacks. Proposed high-level plan (attached detailed checklist):

- Week 0 (this week): configuration and staging — exchange SP metadata, create test IdP app, collect SCIM service account credentials.
- Week 1: SCIM staging run (read-only) and SAML integration in sandbox; validate claims and group mappings.
- Week 2: SAML go/no-go + IP allowlist dry-run (traffic mirroring), followed by production cutover in a 1-hour maintenance window.

Critical asks from FinVault for scheduling:
- Confirm two-hour maintenance windows in UTC-7 on Tue/Wed next week.
- Provide the public IP ranges (or CIDR list) your egress uses for the cutover.
- Share service account credentials for SCIM (we recommend a scoped, non-interactive service account).

Attachments: scim-staging-checklist.xlsx, saml-fallback-diagram.png, ip-allowlist-template.csv

I'll coordinate owners: Jonas will lead the technical runbook and fallback wiring; Marissa will handle CS day-of operations and comms; Ben will track commercial approvals. Next step: James, can you confirm the maintenance windows and share the CIDRs by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,

Naomi Feldman

Thanks James — perfect. Quick answers inline: 

- Maintenance window: we’ll tentatively book Tue 2028-06-12 01:00–03:00 UTC-7 (Naomi to send calendar invite once you confirm).
- SCIM service account scope: yes — we support scoped SCIM tokens. Please provide a key that can write Users and Groups only; we will not request broader org-level entitlements.
- SAML fallback behavior: see high-level flow below and attached diagram (saml-fallback-diagram.png):
  - Normal: SP -> IdP assertion accepted -> user proceeds to app.
  - IdP failure / assertion error: SP will detect the failure and (a) surface a branded error with both Redwood + FinVault support contacts, and (b) present an option to use a one-time backup login (if you prefer we can enable an emergency helpdesk token flow).
  - If you prefer a legacy fallback (username/password), we can enable it for a narrow subset of users (e.g., support accounts) for the first 72 hours post-cutover.

Next steps (owners):
- FinVault: confirm final CIDR list and SCIM key by EOD 2028-06-05.
- Jonas: produce runbook sections for SAML assertion verification and emergency rollback steps.
- Marissa: draft comms for end-users and support teams (T-3 days, T-0 day).

Naomi

On Mon, Jun 4, 2028 at 11:28 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Jonas: produce runbook sections for SAML assertion verification and emergency rollback steps.

Adding technical detail for the runbook and the SCIM staging window:

Runbook highlights (to be included in the drive doc):
- Pre-cutover checks (T-2h): verify IdP cert chain, validate SP metadata, run assertion-test suite against a sample account, ensure SCIM write completes for a test group.
- Cutover steps (T-0 to T+30m): set IP allowlist entries, switch SP endpoints from sandbox to prod, monitor 5xx/401 spikes for first 15 minutes.
- Emergency rollback (T+30m): revert IP allowlist to previous baseline, flip SP endpoint back to sandbox, and invalidate any new SCIM changes made during the interval if necessary.

SAML fallback mechanics:
- We will instrument the SP to emit a specific fallback event code (rw.saml.fallback) so your SREs can trigger a synthetic check and automate rollback if user error rates exceed threshold X (suggested 5% error rate for 15 minutes).

Service accounts / SCIM notes:
- Use a JWT-based service account key with rotation window 90 days. Keep it scoped to Users/Groups.
- We’ll provide a staging tenant where we run a dry-write with a limited user set (5 test accounts) — this avoids global changes until you confirm.

I’ll draft the runbook and post the link to the Drive doc by EOD.

-Jonas
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
